name: Abū Bishr ʿAmr ibn ʿUthmān ibn Qanbar Sībawayh
summary: The Basran grammarian whose al-Kitāb, the first written grammar of Arabic, became the reference of every later book of naḥw and ṣarf.
bio: Sībawayh was a Persian client, born, al-Zubaydī says, in al-Bayḍāʾ, a village of the province of Shiraz. He came to Basra to write down hadith in the circle of Ḥammād ibn Salama, and grammar, by the story al-Zubaydī tells, came to him through a mistake: reading out a hadith with the words laysa Abā al-Dardāʾ, he corrected it to laysa Abū al-Dardāʾ, and Ḥammād told him he was wrong, since laysa here is a particle of exception. 'I shall seek a knowledge in which you cannot fault me,' Sībawayh said, and he joined al-Khalīl. He learnt also from Yūnus ibn Ḥabīb, ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar and al-Akhfash al-Akbar. His name is Persian; al-Zubaydī explains it as 'thirty scents', others as 'scent of apples'.

In Baghdad he met the Kufan al-Kisāʾī, tutor of the caliph's sons, before the Barmakid vizier Yaḥyā ibn Khālid. The story of that meeting, the masʾala zunbūriyya, is told in several versions (al-Zubaydī gives three): al-Kisāʾī asked whether one says 'I thought the scorpion stung harder than the hornet, and lo, it is he (fa-idhā huwa hiya)' or 'and lo, it is her (fa-idhā huwa iyyāhā)'. Sībawayh allowed only the first; al-Kisāʾī allowed both. Bedouin waiting at the door were called in and sided with al-Kisāʾī; Sībawayh was given ten thousand dirhams and left Iraq. Sībawayh's followers, al-Zubaydī adds, have always held that his answer was right, and that the Bedouin were men al-Kisāʾī knew and relied on. He went to Persia and died there young, by al-Zubaydī's account at thirty-three, in 180/796; the reports say grief had a part in it.

His one work has no title: later scholars call it simply al-Kitāb, the Book, or 'the Qurʾān of grammar'. It treats syntax, then morphology and phonology, quoting al-Khalīl, Yūnus and the speech and poetry of the Arabs. No one read it with him; it was handed on by his student al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ, and every later Basran, from al-Mubarrad to al-Sīrāfī, wrote on it.

works.title: al-Kitāb
works.note: The first comprehensive grammar of Arabic.

reception: Al-Kitāb was commented on by al-Mubarrad, Ibn al-Sarrāj, al-Sīrāfī, al-Rummānī and many others; later handbooks are summaries of it more often than they say.
uncertain: His year of death is given between 161/778 and 194/810; 180/796 is the most common.
The details of the masʾala zunbūriyya differ in each version, and later grammarians defended both answers.
